common_name: Cranberry Cocktail Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Deep Red Sempervivum)

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun in spring or fall.

directions: Cranberry Cocktail is part of Chris Hansen's Chick Charms breeding program and forms tight rosettes of deep wine-red to maroon leaves that intensify toward near-black at the tips under strong sun and cool weather. Plant in lean, gritty, fast-draining soil in full sun, since shaded plants fade to duller green-red and lose the saturated color the cultivar is grown for. Like other hens and chicks, the mother rosette sends out short stolons tipped with offset chicks that root quickly, slowly filling in a rock garden pocket or shallow container. An occasional mature rosette will bolt a thick flower stalk in summer and decline afterward, but the surrounding offsets carry the clump on without interruption.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens Chick Charms catalog

common_name: Lemon Waves Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Ruffled Chartreuse Sempervivum)

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun in spring or fall.

directions: Lemon Waves is distinguished within the Chick Charms line by heavily ruffled, undulating leaf margins in bright chartreuse-yellow that catch light differently than the smooth-edged rosettes typical of most hens and chicks. Grow in lean, mineral, sharply drained soil in full sun to keep the ruffling pronounced and the color vivid, since rich soil or shade produces looser, greener growth. The rosette stays compact at only a few inches across and multiplies by short-stemmed offset chicks that can be detached and replanted once rooted. Winter cold deepens the yellow toward a warm gold before the plant resumes active growth in spring.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens Chick Charms catalog

common_name: Glacier Blue Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Powdery Blue-Grey Sempervivum)

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun in spring or fall.

directions: Glacier Blue carries a powdery, frosted blue-grey leaf color across tight, symmetrical rosettes, part of the Chick Charms breeding line selected for unusual pigment and texture in cold-hardy sempervivums. Full sun and lean, sharply drained gravelly soil keep the glaucous coating intact and the color at its coolest, since overwatering or shade can wash the rosette toward plain green. Established clumps spread slowly as the mother rosette produces offset chicks on short stolons that root into the surrounding soil or gravel mulch. Hardy well below freezing, it needs no winter protection in climates with well-drained soil, but standing winter moisture is the most common cause of rot.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens Chick Charms catalog

planting.note: Root offsets or leaf cuttings in spring in very well-drained, gritty succulent mix in full sun to bright indoor light; as a named intergeneric hybrid it is propagated strictly vegetatively.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, gritty succulent mix in full sun or bright indoor light, letting the soil dry completely between waterings. 'Lovely Rose' forms small, tight rosettes under five inches tall that blush a soft rosy-pink across the leaf tips and margins when grown in strong light, fading toward pale green-grey in lower light. It stays compact compared to many Graptoveria hybrids, making it well suited to small pots and dish gardens, and offsets readily from the base to form a tidy cluster. Protect from temperatures below about 30 degrees F, since this is a soft, frost-tender succulent best grown outdoors only in mild winter climates or brought indoors for winter elsewhere.

planting.note: Root offsets or leaf cuttings in spring in very well-drained, gritty succulent mix in full sun to bright light; as a named hybrid it does not come true from seed, so all propagation is vegetative.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, gritty succulent mix in full sun to bright light, watering deeply and then allowing the mix to dry fully before watering again. 'Inti Platense' forms open rosettes of thick, pointed leaves in muted lavender-grey tones that pick up pink to coppery blush along the margins under strong sun and cool nights. It offsets from the base to slowly form a small clump rather than trailing, and leaves that detach cleanly will root and grow into new plantlets. Keep it above roughly 30 degrees F, since it has no tolerance for hard frost and is grown as a container or mild-climate landscape succulent.

planting.note: Root offsets or leaf cuttings in spring in very well-drained, gritty succulent mix in full sun to bright indoor light; as a named hybrid it is propagated strictly vegetatively.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, gritty succulent mix in full sun or bright indoor light, letting the mix dry out completely between waterings to prevent rot. 'Draco' forms small, chunky rosettes of thick, pointed leaves that stay under about five inches tall and four inches across, with coloring that shifts from blue-green to a warmer bronze-pink under intense light. It clumps slowly by basal offsets, keeping a dense, compact habit well suited to shallow pots and mixed succulent bowls. This soft-leaved hybrid has no frost tolerance below about 30 degrees F and should be grown as a container plant outside of mild, frost-free climates.

planting.note: Root offsets or leaf cuttings in spring in very well-drained, gritty succulent mix in full sun to bright light; as a named Japanese-origin hybrid it is propagated strictly vegetatively.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, gritty succulent mix in full sun to bright light, watering thoroughly and then waiting for the soil to dry fully before the next watering. 'Hanabijin', whose Japanese name translates roughly to "fireworks beauty," forms chunky, pointed-leaf rosettes with a soft powdery coating that flushes pink to coral at the leaf tips under bright, cool-season light. It offsets modestly from the base rather than trailing, building a compact clump over a few growing seasons. Handle leaves carefully since rubbing removes the powdery bloom permanently, and protect from temperatures below about 30 degrees F as this soft succulent has essentially no frost tolerance.
